svg.title: Nimbus input preparation, owned pixel predictions and whole-cell decisions
svg.desc: The first row prepares two inputs at model magnification 10x. One marker is divided by the complete image positive-pixel 0.999 quantile and clipped to zero through one, then sampled linearly. Original cell IDs are converted to binary interiors by removing four-neighbour inner boundaries, then sampled with nearest neighbours. The matched pixel grids retain the same three cell IDs and coordinates. The second row sends a two-plane 1024-square input with a 96-pixel halo through fixed Nimbus V1. The 836-square score prediction loses two pixels on every edge to own 832-square pixels. The right-edge inset enlarges exactly the eight indicated score columns. Six views are restored to original image coordinates. A separate route retains the original whole-cell masks, including boundary pixels. The six-row sample lattice explains which values enter the displayed mean; it does not imply an allocated dense buffer. Each original cell pixel contributes once per view and the denominator is six times its pixel count. Cell scores meet a reviewed cutoff c to produce y_i. The optional intensity fit pairs finite measurements and known decisions by cell ID and minimizes hard-label disagreements. The ordered example has two disagreements among twelve cells. Grid intensities, scores and the threshold example are schematic.
